idea-plugin.name: Emberkai Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Emberkai is a warm, high-color dark theme for IntelliJ-based IDEs, with a light variant.

Built on the Islands layout, with a Contrast option for brighter comments and secondary text, Teal, Rose, and Ember accents, and a Light theme on warm paper backgrounds. Buttons, run and stop controls, badges, and file icons all follow the same palette.

Includes optional No Italics editor schemes, coordinated diff and console colors, and palette-matched semantic highlighting for parameters and local variables. Semantic highlighting is off by default.

Requires IntelliJ Platform 2026.1 or newer. Select a theme under Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Appearance.

Report an issue | Source code | Apache 2.0 license

Theme color credits: Neokai by tautastic and Monokai Pro Theme 1.10 by Subtheme.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.1.0 — New light theme.

  • New Emberkai Islands Light with warm paper backgrounds, a bright orange accent, and the dark palette's syntax color roles.
  • New Emberkai Light and Emberkai Light - No Italics editor schemes with matching diff, console, and semantic highlighting colors.

2.0.5 — Search highlights, scrollbars, and readability fixes.

  • Find results in the editor are tinted yellow, and highlighted usages are blue for reads and rose for writes. Both are marked in the scrollbar, as are breakpoints.
  • The matched text highlight in Search Everywhere, trees, and lists follows the Teal, Rose, and Ember accents instead of staying yellow.
  • Non-project and test files have a faint tint. The yellow tint looked like the selected row.
  • Indeterminate progress bars animate again, split editors have a visible divider, and editor scrollbars brighten on hover.
  • Runtime errors, duplicated code, Presentation Assistant popups, progress counters, plugin tags, and disabled fields are visible or readable.

2.0.4 — Support for IntelliJ Platform 2026.3.

  • The tool window drop hint added in 2026.3 uses the accent instead of JetBrains blue.

2.0.3 — Readability and contrast fixes across the editor and UI.

  • Unused, deprecated, disabled, and unresolved code has its own muted color instead of looking like a comment. Comments, line numbers, whitespace, and indent guides are easier to see, and the selection keeps text readable.
  • Muted text, disabled text, and previously near-invisible Grammar-Kit, JFlex, and .ignore elements are brighter.
  • Buttons, segmented controls, tool window tabs, popups, menus, balloons, checkboxes, and badge dots follow the palette and accent instead of Darcula grays and blues.
  • The code completion selection, Git-ignored files, and parameter hints are easier to read.

2.0.2 — New Ember accent, and the last Darcula colors replaced with the palette.

  • New Emberkai Islands Ember accent: a light ember orange, kept distinct from the warning color.
  • Editor colors that still came from Darcula now use the palette, including inlay hints, unmatched braces, grammar underlines, regular expressions, debugger, terminal blocks, and diagrams.
  • Bundled plugin colors follow the palette: SQL, Kotlin, Angular, Compose, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, code review, Code With Me, and find usages.
  • RustRover lifetimes, type parameters, macros, mutable bindings, and unsafe, disabled, and generated code use palette colors.

2.0.1 — First Marketplace release of 2.0, with the 2.0.0 changes below.

2.0.0 — Emberkai now has a single palette.

  • Breaking: the Default, Machine, Octagon, and Ristretto palettes are removed. Themes are now Emberkai Islands, Contrast, Teal, and Rose. Reselect the editor scheme under Settings > Editor > Color Scheme if it resets.
  • Run and stop buttons, plugin buttons, toggles, banners, badges, and progress bars use the palette instead of Islands' stock green and red.
  • Editor colors previously copied from other themes now come from the palette, including parameters, constants, rainbow brackets, TODOs, breakpoints, and coverage.
  • Unused code uses the comment color, and the Rose accent no longer matches errors.
  • Test and non-project file colors, plus more Symbols icons, follow the palette.
